title: Negative: adding uniform chemical turnover (-eps(phi - phi_t)) to active Model H freezes droplets into a static microphase array; activity only adds a few rods, no division cycle
summary: Screen on seed 0 (128^2, t=1500, quick.py) of the active-model-h sighting world with a Model-A turnover toward phi_t=-0.4 (material made outside droplets, removed inside). eps=0.001 and 0.003 with zeta=0 both arrest coarsening at a fixed droplet size (the known Ohta-Kawasaki microphase, a near-hexagonal array at eps=0.003); with zeta=-1 the arrays look the same except for a few elongated rods at eps=0.001. Nothing grows past the arrest size, so the active elongation never gets a growing droplet to split, and flows stay ~4e-3. A uniform relaxation term is the wrong chemistry for growth-and-division: droplets need net growth from a supersaturated outside and an internal sink (Zwicker-type), which this term does not provide at these rates.

finding.operator: Model-A turnover -eps(phi - phi_t) added to active Model H
finding.control: zeta=0 vs zeta=-1 at eps=0.001 and 0.003, same seed and grid
finding.result: static arrested arrays at both eps with or without activity; at eps=0.001, zeta=-1 adds a few rods; no repeated division; one seed, screen only
